requirements.text: On every day the NYSE is open, calculate the Fund's NAV as of the close of regular NYSE trading, or as of the actual early close when applicable.
requirements.quote: USBFS... calculates the Fund’s NAV at the close of regular trading (ordinarily 4:00 p.m. E.S.T.) every day the New York Stock Exchange is open... If the NYSE closes early on a valuation day, the Funds shall determine NAV as of that time.

requirements.text: Maintain each FLEX option by underlying ETF, call or put, purchased or written status, European exercise style, strike, expiration date, contract quantity, contract multiplier, trade-date cost or premium, and current value. For these tests, apply a multiplier of 100 shares per contract.
requirements.quote: The FLEX Options in which the Fund invests are all European style option contracts... Footnotes to the options: Exchange-traded. 100 shares per contract.

requirements.text: Record option purchases on trade date as investments at premium paid, including capitalizable transaction costs, and subsequently mark them to current value.
requirements.quote: Investment transactions are recorded on the trade date... When the Funds purchase an option, an amount equal to the premium paid by the Funds are recorded as an investment and is subsequently adjusted to the current value of the option purchased.

requirements.text: Record written options on trade date as liabilities at premium received and subsequently mark the liabilities to current value. Do not offset purchased-option assets against written-option liabilities on the balance sheet.
requirements.quote: When the Funds write an option, an amount equal to the premium received by the Funds are recorded as a liability and is subsequently adjusted to the current value of the option written... All of the FLEX Option contracts held by the Funds are fully funded and cash settled, therefore balance sheet offsetting under U.S. GAAP does not apply.

requirements.text: Value a FLEX option at its same-day market trading price when one exists; otherwise use the exchange's model-based price at the exchange's official close.
requirements.quote: FLEX Options listed on an exchange will typically be valued at a model-based price provided by the exchange at the official close of that exchange’s trading day. However, when the Fund’s option has a same-day market trading price, this same-day market trading price will be used... instead of the exchange’s model-based price.

requirements.text: If the exchange does not provide a FLEX model price, use the backup third-party provider's model price. If an applicable pricing vendor is unavailable, obtain a value from Innovator as Valuation Designee under the valuation procedures.
requirements.quote: If the exchange on which the option is traded is unable to provide a model price, model-based FLEX Options prices will additionally be provided by a backup third-party pricing provider... If either pricing vendor is not available to provide a model price for that day, the value of a FLEX option will be determined by Innovator as Valuation Designee in accordance with the Valuation Procedures.

requirements.text: Obtain the client's approved operational definition of 'same-day market trading price,' including whether the Fund's own trade controls, which trade controls when there are multiple trades, and whether trades occurring before or after an exchange model or settlement publication are treated differently.
requirements.quote: When the Fund’s option has a same-day market trading price, this same-day market trading price will be used...
requirements.assumption_or_question: Ask the client and Valuation Designee for the approved price-source hierarchy and multiple-trade convention before configuring production valuation.

requirements.text: When the same FLEX option appears in both an all-cash basket and an in-kind basket on the same trading day, use the trade price for both instances instead of using a model price for the in-kind transaction.
requirements.quote: In instances where in the same trading day, a particular FLEX Option is represented in an all-cash basket... as well as in an in-kind basket... the Fund will default to use the trade price for both instances, rather than the model price otherwise available for the in-kind transaction.

requirements.text: Calculate purchased-option unrealized gain or loss as current value less identified cost. Calculate written-option unrealized gain or loss as premium received less the current liability value. Post daily changes through the Fund's derivative gain or loss accounts.
requirements.quote: When the Funds purchase an option... [it] is subsequently adjusted to the current value... When the Funds write an option... [the liability] is subsequently adjusted to the current value... The Trust determines the gain or loss realized from investment transactions on the basis of identified cost.

requirements.text: For a purchased option sold or closed before expiration, remove the identified cost of the contracts closed and recognize proceeds less that cost and applicable brokerage commission as realized gain or loss. For a written option bought back, recognize allocated premium received less repurchase price and brokerage commission as realized gain or loss.
requirements.quote: If an option expires... or if the Funds enter into a closing sale transaction, a gain or loss is realized... The difference between the premium and the amount paid on effecting a closing purchase transaction, including brokerage commissions, is also treated as a realized gain, or... realized loss.

requirements.text: Configure identified-lot processing for partial option disposals and require a valid lot election or approved default method when more than one opening lot exists.
requirements.quote: The Trust determines the gain or loss realized from investment transactions on the basis of identified cost.
requirements.assumption_or_question: Ask the client which lot-selection method applies when no specific lot instruction is received; identified cost does not itself specify FIFO, LIFO, highest cost, or another default.

requirements.text: At expiration, cash-settle each option using its intrinsic value: call equals max(reference closing price minus strike, zero) times the applicable multiplier and contracts; put equals max(strike minus reference closing price, zero) times the multiplier and contracts. Purchased options generate cash receivable; written options generate cash payable. Remove all expired positions and recognize realized gain or loss against their cost or premium.
requirements.quote: Cash-settled option contracts give the holder the right to receive an amount (or owe an amount) of cash... The amount of cash is equal to the difference between the closing price of the Reference Asset’s price return and the exercise price of the option contract times a specified multiple... Option contracts that expire unexercised have no value.

requirements.text: At the conclusion of an Outcome Period, settle all expiring FLEX options in cash, close the old series, and book the new approximately one-year FLEX series on its trade date as the next Outcome Period begins.
requirements.quote: Upon conclusion of the Outcome Period, the Fund will receive the cash value of all the FLEX Options it held for the prior Outcome Period. It will then invest in a new series of FLEX Options with an expiration date of approximately one year in the future.

requirements.text: Do not accrue dividend income merely because the reference ETF goes ex-dividend when the Fund holds only FLEX options. Mark the options to their ex-date values, because the strategy receives price return rather than the reference ETF's dividends.
requirements.quote: If the Fund invests solely in FLEX Options that reference the Underlying ETF... returns will be provided based on changes in the share price of the Underlying ETF, and the Fund will not receive the benefit of any dividends.

requirements.text: Accrue the 0.79% annual unitary management fee daily based on average daily net assets and record the unpaid accrual as a liability; settle it monthly.
requirements.quote: The Fund has agreed to pay an annual unitary management fee... equal to 0.79% of its average daily net assets... pay monthly the Adviser a unitary fee calculated daily based on the average daily net assets... at the annual rate of 0.79%.

requirements.text: Obtain and configure the fee accrual day-count basis and the precise definition of average daily net assets, including treatment of weekends, holidays, subscriptions, redemptions, and same-day market movements.
requirements.quote: A unitary fee calculated daily based on the average daily net assets... at the annual rate of 0.79%.
requirements.assumption_or_question: The documents do not specify a 365/366-day convention or the intraday averaging method.

requirements.text: Accrue MMDA interest using the applicable daily variable rate and the custodian's approved balance and day-count convention, including calendar-day accrual over weekends.
requirements.quote: The MMDA will bear interest at a variable rate that is determined based on market conditions and is subject to change daily.

requirements.text: Obtain the MMDA's contractual day-count basis, compounding convention, rate-effective time, and treatment of weekends and holidays from the custodian before production configuration.
requirements.quote: The MMDA will bear interest at a variable rate...
requirements.assumption_or_question: The public documents do not specify these interest-calculation conventions.

requirements.text: Calculate net assets as total current assets, including accrued income, less all liabilities. Divide by shares outstanding and publish NAV per share rounded to the nearest cent.
requirements.quote: The NAV for one Share... is calculated by taking the market price of the Fund’s total assets, including any interest or dividends accrued but not yet collected, less all liabilities, and dividing such amount by the total number of Shares outstanding. The result, rounded to the nearest cent is the NAV per Share.

requirements.text: Process Creation Unit orders at the applicable NAV. For creations, issue shares and receive the NAV consideration plus the transaction fee. For redemptions, cancel shares and deliver instruments plus or minus balancing cash, less the redemption fee and other applicable charges. A stated transaction fee applies once per order regardless of the number of units in that order.
requirements.quote: Creation Units are sold at their NAV plus a transaction fee... A transaction fee is applicable to each transaction regardless of the number of units purchased or sold in the transaction.

requirements.text: For an in-kind basket, calculate the Cash Component or Cash Redemption Amount as NAV per Creation Unit minus the aggregate net market value of the instruments. Retain the applicable transaction fee for the Fund and recognize realized gain or loss on options transferred in kind using identified cost.
requirements.quote: The Cash Component is an amount equal to the difference between the NAV of a Fund’s shares (per Creation Unit) and the Deposit Amount... The redemption proceeds... consist of the Deposit Instruments... plus or minus cash... less the applicable Redemption Transaction Fee... Amount is included in realized gain/(loss) in-kind.

requirements.text: Obtain the operational rule for converting fractional pro-rata option quantities into whole-contract basket quantities, including rounding direction and cash-in-lieu treatment.
requirements.quote: When utilizing a pro-rata basket, minor deviations may occur when it is not operationally feasible to include a particular instrument within the basket.
requirements.assumption_or_question: The documents permit minor deviations but do not prescribe whether 60.6 contracts must be rounded to 60, rounded to 61, or handled through a custom basket.

requirements.text: Apply OCC or clearing-broker corporate-action adjustments to contract quantities, strikes, multipliers, and deliverables on the effective date, and reconcile the adjusted position to the clearing record before NAV.
requirements.quote: FLEX Options... are guaranteed for settlement by the Options Clearing Corporation (OCC).
requirements.assumption_or_question: Ask OCC or the clearing broker for the authoritative adjustment terms for each split or other reference-ETF corporate action; the documents do not specify the adjustment algorithm.

requirements.text: Maintain a stale-price and NAV-error control that compares each day's loaded FLEX price with the current approved source, quantifies the dollar and per-share effect of any error, and routes errors under the Fund's correction policy.
requirements.assumption_or_question: Ask the client for its NAV-error materiality threshold, correction methodology, shareholder reimbursement rules, and escalation requirements; none are stated in the supplied documents.
